Hi Emily,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is a concise security architecture snapshot that maps our Dedicated and Private deployment isolation boundaries for your review (see attachment: acme-network-diagram-v2.pdf). Highlights:

- Private deployment uses an isolated control plane with customer-managed VPC peering (no shared control plane metadata).
- Dedicated pools are tenant-fenced at the hyperplane layer; KV cache and runtime are namespace-separated.
- Egress paths are restricted via customer-specific NATs and proxy ACLs; we publish per-tenant egress allowlists for auditing.

Action items for you: please confirm which questionnaire you want prioritized (SIG Lite, SIG Full, CAIQ). We can produce a SIG/CAIQ mapping spreadsheet and an evidence index — draft attached will be ready in 48 hours once you confirm scope.

Proposed timeline:
- 2 business days: SIG/CAIQ mapping draft (spreadsheet)
- 5 business days: compiled evidence packet (PDF + artifacts)
- 7–10 business days: delivery and follow-up call to walk through attestation items

Attachment(s): acme-network-diagram-v2.pdf

If you want a very short summary for procurement, I can send a one-page control summary.

Best,

Emily —

Quick answers inline:

1) SOC 2 scope: Redwood's SOC 2 Type II covers our hosted control plane and the managed services we operate on Redwood-infrastructure. For Private deployments placed into a customer's VPC (customer-managed networking), we provide a scoped attestation addendum that documents which controls remain in-scope (e.g., our runtime code push process, key management interactions) and which are transferred to the customer (network-level segmentation, VPC ACLs). I attached a short evidence-index.pdf that shows typical breakpoints.

2) Air-gapped option: we do not currently offer a fully air-gapped runtime that operates without any outbound connectivity for model telemetry/patching in our standard offering. For regulated customers we provide:
- an airlock operating mode: no default telemetry; controlled update windows via signed offline bundles delivered through an approved transfer channel;
- on-demand offline evidence packs (signed logs, signed config snapshots) delivered via SFTP/NDA;
- option for an on-prem maintenance contract where we ship signed binaries and run a supervised patching cadence under customer oversight.

We will mark each SIG/CAIQ line item in the mapping as: Available, NDA required, or On-site validation required. Draft mapping (sig-caiq-mapping-draft.xlsx) and network-legend.txt attached.

Next steps: I’ll hand this to Kimberly to populate the control-level mappings and indicate which artifacts are extractable from our evidence store vs. which require manual collection. Can we target Tue 9/16 for the annotated mapping?

Best,
Ben

Hi Emily / Ben —

Kimberly here (Security Architect) — I updated the mapping to include per-control evidence locations and short notes for auditor consumption. Key clarifications below and included in the attached PDF: sig-caiq-mapping-annotated.pdf (inline excerpts pasted as well).

A. Control boundary clarifications (short):
- Control plane (management) telemetry: for Private deployments the control plane runs in a RedHat container in the customer VPC but the control plane admin API is authenticated with a mutual-TLS certificate issued by Redwood's CA; root-level logs are MD-signed and available via our evidence store on request.
- Data plane (inference): tenant model inputs/outputs only traverse the customer VPC to the dedicated runtime. No shared storage of customer prompts on the hosted model catalog.
- KMS interactions: customer can bring their own KMS (BYOK) for encryption-at-rest keys; when BYOK is used, Redwood logs the KMS key ID but never stores raw key material.

B. Evidence packaging approach:
- Available now: service configuration snapshots, signed runtime hashes, SOC 2 report (hosted), encryption config extracts.
- NDA required: deeper forensic logs, internal process runbooks, vulnerability scan raw output.
- On-site validation: hardware control plane checks and sealed-bundle verification.

C. Proposed delivery cadence for Acme:
- Tue 9/16: annotated SIG/CAIQ mapping (spreadsheet + short narrative)
- Thu 9/18: compiled evidence packet (PDF + attachments) delivered via SFTP (NDA in place)
- Mon 9/22: walkthrough call with auditors (1 hour)

Attachment(s): sig-caiq-mapping-annotated.pdf

If that schedule works, we'll stage the SFTP endpoint and send an NDA template to procurement.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
